lines.beaver: 오늘 제사에 대해 알려 주실 수 있어요?
lines.beaver_en: Could you tell me about jesa today?
lines.beaver_roman: Oneul jesae daehae allyeo jusil su isseoyo?
lines.learner: 네, 제사는 돌아가신 조상을 기억하는 의식이에요.
lines.en: Sure, jesa is a rite to remember our late ancestors.
lines.roman: Ne, jesaneun doragasin josangeul gieokaneun uisigieyo.

lines.beaver_en: Is it related to faith, then? Is it a religion?
lines.en: It's closer to a cultural tradition than a religious rite.

lines.beaver_en: Do ancestors become gods? Like ghosts?
lines.en: Long ago, people believed ancestors' spirits came to visit.

lines.beaver_en: How do people see it now?
lines.en: Now we think of it as a day when family gathers.

lines.beaver_en: What do you put on the memorial table?
lines.learner: 과일이며 떡이며 전이며 음식을 많이 올려요.
lines.en: We put lots of food: fruit, rice cakes, pancakes and more.
lines.roman: Gwairimyeo tteogimyeo jeonimyeo eumsigeul mani ollyeoyo.

lines.beaver: 와, 맛있겠네요. 교회 다니는 분도 지내요?
lines.beaver_en: Wow, sounds tasty. Do churchgoers hold it too?
lines.beaver_roman: Wa, masitgenneyo. Gyohoe danineun bundo jinaeyo?
lines.learner: 집마다 달라요. 안 지내는 집도 있어요.
lines.en: It depends on the family. Some don't hold it.
lines.roman: Jimmada dallayo. An jinaeneun jipdo isseoyo.

lines.beaver_en: Then what do those families do?
lines.en: They hold a memorial service as a family.

lines.beaver_en: What about people who go to temple?
lines.learner: 부처님을 믿는 집은 절에서 제사를 지내기도 해요.
lines.en: Families who follow the Buddha sometimes hold it at a temple.
lines.roman: Bucheonimeul minneun jibeun jeoreseo jesareul jinaegido haeyo.

lines.beaver_en: So each faith has its own way.
lines.learner: 신앙이 달라도 가족이 함께 모이는 게 중요해요.
lines.en: Even with different faiths, family gathering together matters.
lines.roman: Sinangi dallado gajogi hamkke moineun ge jungyohaeyo.

lines.beaver: 설명 고마워요. 이번 추석에 꼭 보고 싶어요.
lines.beaver_en: Thanks for explaining. I'd love to see it this Chuseok.
lines.beaver_roman: Seolmyeong gomawoyo. Ibeon chuseoge kkok bogo sipeoyo.
lines.en: Great. I'll invite you to our family's jesa.
